transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My regular doctor told me I had to come. He says I've gotten too thin. I mean... I can see my work pants hanging loose on me, I guess. But... I don't know. Part of me still feels relieved when the number on the scale is lower. So... he sent me here.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I... suppose so. It's just... if I have something heavier, you know, like a biscuit or some pasta... I just worry. I spend the rest of the day scared it's going to show on me. I end up checking myself a lot... just thinking I need to make up for it somehow. That's all.
Do you think you look fat even when others say you're too thin?

I don't know about "fat," exactly. It's just... I like things to be neat. When I stay small, it just feels like... like I'm handling everything right. Keeping it all in order. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full... I just feel like I've let myself go. Like I'm not trying hard enough.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
No... I don't do that. I wouldn't really want to eat a lot at once. I just... stick to what I know.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No. I... I don't do that. I just... I just don't eat much in the first place, so there's no need for that.
Do you exercise a lot to burn off calories?
No... I don't really do that. I'm a cleaner, so I'm on my feet most of the day for work anyway. I don't... go out of my way to exercise on top of that.
Do you think your weight is a problem even when others tell you that you are underweight?

I wouldn't call it a problem. People say what they want, but... I just like things a certain way. When I stay small and... neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. If I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full, I just... I feel like I've let myself go. So I just try to avoid that.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you thought was too much in a short period of time?
No. I... I don't really do that. Like I said, I just... I don't eat much to begin with. So, no.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while you're eating?
No... I don't. Like I said, I keep things pretty small. So... I always know exactly what I'm having. I don't lose control.
Do you think your weight is a big part of how you evaluate yourself as a person?

I suppose... I mean, it's just like I was saying before. Keeping myself small and... neat... it just makes me feel like I'm doing things right. If I look in the mirror and see any fullness at all, I just feel like I've let myself go. So... yes. I guess it is.
Is there a specific weight or body shape that you are trying to maintain?
I... I don't really have a specific number in mind. I just... I just want to keep things the way they are. Small. I don't know exactly what weight that is.
Do you think you would still want to be as thin as you are now if everyone around you told you that you look healthy and fine at a slightly higher weight?

I... probably. It doesn't really matter what other people say. Like I told you just a minute ago... it's about how I feel. If I see my stomach looking full in the mirror, I'm still going to feel like I let myself go, even if someone else thinks I look fine. Staying small is just... how I know I'm handling things.
Do you feel like being thin helps you feel more in control of your life in general?

I... I don't know if I'd call it control. It's just... like I keep saying. When I manage to stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. If my stomach looks the least bit full in the mirror, I just feel like I've let myself go. That's really all it is.
Is your main goal in restricting your food intake to avoid gaining weight or to feel more in control of your body?

I... I guess it's mostly about the weight. Like, if I eat something heavier... maybe biscuits or pasta... I just spend the rest of the day scared it's going to show on me. I end up checking the mirror a lot. Just... thinking about how I need to make up for it. I just don't want to get bigger.
Is avoiding weight gain the main reason you restrict what you eat?

Yes... like I just said. It's the weight. If I have something heavy, I just... I worry it's going to show on me right away. Then I'm stuck checking myself all day, trying to figure out how to make up for it. So... yes, I just avoid it.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered normal, but then felt like you had lost control and eaten too much?
No... I don't think so. I don't really lose control like that. I just... stick to what I plan to have. That's all.
Have you ever had a time when you ate a normal amount of food, but then felt extremely full and like you had eaten too much?
No... not really. Like I just said before, I just stick to my plan. I don't really eat enough to feel... extremely full like that. I just have what I'm used to having.
Have you ever had times when you ate much more than you normally would in a short period of time?
No. I don't do that. I just... I keep it controlled. I don't eat a lot at once.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt like you were eating an unusually large amount of food in a short time?
No... I think we just went over this. It's like I said before, I just don't eat like that.
